summary: Jefferson County, MT summit lookout; sources disagree on its date, and a hiking blog describes only a stone base left on the summit.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a stone base
facts.status_note: Listed as ruins by firelookout.com and firelookout.org; a 2023 hiking blog describes a stone structure on the summit with its wooden upper story gone

access.note: Hikers reach the summit on foot by trail from the Casey Meadows Trailhead; no closure or permission rule found in the sources read

visit.trail_note: Trail begins at the Casey Meadows Trailhead, a 16-mile drive from Helena (hiking blog)

events.note: June 1937 newspaper item, reprinted by Forest Lookouts, announced a planned lookout station on High peak with a 20-foot log tower; the item itself does not name Casey Peak

evidence.supports: page places the site in the Helena National Forest
page heading for the site is Casey Peak
1937 item announces a new lookout station on High peak at the head of McClellan Creek
evidence.quote: on top of High peak at the head of McClellan creek

evidence.supports: planned 20-foot log tower with a glassed-in lookout house
evidence.quote: A 20-foot log tower with a glassed in lookout house will be constructed on the peak

evidence.supports: station to be set up around the first of July
evidence.quote: the lookout station will be set up probably about the first of July

evidence.supports: the article describes High peak, not Casey Peak
evidence.quote: High peak is situated on the divide between McClellan creek

evidence.supports: stone first floor of a lookout used briefly in the early 1900s, with a wooden second story above
evidence.quote: the first floor of a fire lookout that was used briefly in the early 1900’s

evidence.supports: wooden upper story has crumbled away
evidence.quote: Its wooden second story with walk-around deck crumbled away several years ago.

evidence.supports: a stone structure sits on the summit
evidence.quote: A curious-looking stone structure sits atop the summit

evidence.supports: trail begins at the Casey Meadows Trailhead, a 16-mile drive from Helena; hikers reach the summit on foot
evidence.quote: The trail to Casey Peak begins at the Casey Meadows Trailhead, a 16-mile drive from Helena.

evidence.supports: trail listing points visitors to the Helena National Forest visitor map
evidence.quote: Area maps available are the Helena National Forest Visitor Map

evidence.supports: 1930s L-4 cab on a stone base; site listed as ruins
evidence.quote: 1930s: L-4 cab on stone base. Ruins.

evidence.supports: firelookout.org list gives status Ruins for Casey Peak in Jefferson county

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com dates an L-4 cab on a stone base to the 1930s; the hiking blog describes the stone first floor as a lookout used briefly in the early 1900s. Both are reported as attributed and neither is confirmed by a third source.

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 6.1 matches the 20-foot tower planned in the 1937 item, not a documented built height, so it is left out of facts for you to decide. Brief kind two_story matches the firelookout.org label '2-Story cab'. Access moves from unknown to public on trail evidence only; no agency closure statement read. The 1937 item names High peak; only the Forest Lookouts page ties it to Casey Peak. The blog links a Helena Independent Record article on the lookout that I did not open. No staffing, fire or rental information found for this site.
